response: The old lighthouse keeper had not seen a ship in twenty years, yet every night he climbed the spiral stairs to light the great lamp. His beard was white, his hands trembled, but the ritual was as steady as the tide. One dawn, a small boat appeared on the horizon, carrying a young woman who claimed the sea had spoken her name in a dream. She handed him a letter, water-stained and yellow, written in his own hand from a youth he barely remembered. It spoke of a promise to guide someone home, and he realized the light had not been for strangers—it had been for her. They sat together on the rocks, watching the waves erase the last trace of her wake, while the keeper finally let the tower go dark.
